intent.raw_query: Swiss Alps ski holiday family, $7000, 7 days, February

experiences.name: Zermatt Ski Safari
experiences.description: Explore the legendary slopes of Zermatt with access to over 360km of groomed pistes beneath the iconic Matterhorn. Take the Gornergrat cogwheel railway to reach high-altitude runs and enjoy varied terrain suitable for all skill levels, with breathtaking panoramic views of 29 peaks over 4000m.

experiences.name: Verbier Freeride Experience
experiences.description: Join a guided off-piste freeride session in Verbier, one of the world's top freeride destinations. A certified mountain guide leads you through untracked powder fields and challenging couloirs in the Mont Fort area, offering an adrenaline-packed adventure for intermediate to advanced skiers.

experiences.name: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Tour
experiences.description: Ride the cogwheel train to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m, the highest railway station in Europe. Explore the Ice Palace carved inside the glacier, walk on the Aletsch Glacier, and enjoy stunning views of the surrounding Alpine peaks. A once-in-a-lifetime mountain experience combining culture and nature.

experiences.name: Swiss Alpine Fondue Evening
experiences.description: Warm up after a day on the slopes with a traditional Swiss cheese fondue dinner at a cozy mountain chalet restaurant in Grindelwald. Enjoy locally sourced Gruyère and Emmental cheeses paired with Swiss wines and regional bread, immersing yourself in authentic Alpine culinary culture.

experiences.name: Davos Cross-Country Skiing & Nordic Trail
experiences.description: Glide through 100km of perfectly groomed Nordic trails around Davos, the highest city in Europe. This full-day cross-country skiing experience takes you through pristine snow-covered forests and frozen lakes, with optional instruction from a local Nordic coach for beginners and intermediates.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich or Milan Malpensa airport at 22:30. Take a pre-booked budget train or bus transfer toward Poschiavo. The Bernina Express or regional rail via Tirano connects to Poschiavo. Check in to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama upon late arrival. Settle in and rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick snack or sandwich from an airport kiosk or train station vending machine (~CHF 5-10) before boarding your transfer

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your train ticket in advance via SBB.ch for the best budget fares. The Poschiavo valley is in the Graubünden canton. Confirm late check-in with the B&B ahead of time. Keep CHF cash handy as rural areas may have limited card acceptance.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from travel. Enjoy a hearty B&B breakfast included with your stay. Take a slow morning walk through the charming historic village of Poschiavo — explore the Piazza Comunale, the Spanish Quarter (Quartiere Spagnolo), and the Church of San Vittore. The village is a UNESCO-listed heritage area and completely free to explore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Lago di Poschiavo (Lake Poschiavo), a short walk or free bus ride from the village center. Walk along the lakeside path enjoying stunning winter mountain views. The frozen or partially frozen lake against the Alpine backdrop is spectacular. Visit the small local shops along Via Principale for budget souvenirs and local Graubünden products.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the village center for a relaxed evening. Explore the local bars and restaurants around Piazza Comunale. Enjoy a warm Graubünden-style dinner at a local trattoria.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — enjoy local bread, cheese, cold cuts, and coffee
meals.lunch: Pick up a local Pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta) or a panino from a village bakery or deli (~CHF 8-12)
meals.dinner: Ristorante Croce Federale or a local trattoria in Poschiavo — try Pizzoccheri della Valtellina or Polenta with local cheese (~CHF 18-25)

day_by_day.notes: Poschiavo has a unique Italian-Swiss cultural blend due to its proximity to Italy. The village is walkable and very budget-friendly. Free village maps are available at the B&B or tourist info point.

day_by_day.morning: Take the iconic Bernina Express (regional train, budget ticket ~CHF 10-15 one way) up toward Ospizio Bernina or Pontresina. The train ride itself through the snow-covered Bernina Pass is one of the most scenic rail journeys in the world — a UNESCO World Heritage route. Arrive at Pontresina, a charming Alpine village and winter sports hub.
day_by_day.afternoon: In Pontresina, explore budget-friendly winter activities. Rent cross-country ski equipment from a local rental shop (~CHF 20-30/day) and use the free or low-cost cross-country ski trails (Langlauf) around Pontresina and the Roseg Valley. The Roseg Valley trail is flat, beginner-friendly, and absolutely stunning with views of glaciers and peaks.
day_by_day.evening: Return by regional train to Poschiavo in the early evening. Warm up with a Glühwein (mulled wine) at a local bar (~CHF 4-6). Cook a simple meal using groceries from the local Coop or Migros supermarket to save money.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from the B&B or buy a sandwich and thermos of soup from a Pontresina bakery (~CHF 8-12)
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner using groceries from Coop Poschiavo — pasta, local cheese, and bread (~CHF 8-12 total)

day_by_day.notes: The Bernina Express regional train is much cheaper than the tourist panoramic version — buy a standard regional ticket on SBB.ch. Cross-country skiing in Pontresina is far more budget-friendly than downhill skiing. Bring your own snacks and a thermos of hot tea to save money on the mountain.

day_by_day.morning: Take the regional Bernina train up to Diavolezza area (alight at Bernina Diavolezza station). Purchase a day ski pass for Diavolezza-Lagalb ski area (~CHF 55-65 for adults — one of the more affordable ski resorts in the Swiss Alps). Rent ski equipment at the base (~CHF 30-40/day). Enjoy morning skiing on well-groomed pistes with incredible views of the Morteratsch Glacier and Piz Palü.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing at Diavolezza. Intermediate and advanced skiers can enjoy the famous off-piste glacier run from Diavolezza to Morteratsch (guided or with experience). Beginners can stick to the blue and red runs. Take a break at the Diavolezza mountain restaurant terrace to soak in the panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Return by train to Poschiavo. Rest tired legs and enjoy a well-deserved dinner at a local restaurant or self-cater at the B&B.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B — eat a big breakfast before a full ski day
meals.lunch: Bring a packed lunch (sandwiches, energy bars, fruit) to avoid expensive mountain restaurant prices — eat at the terrace (~CHF 0 if self-packed vs CHF 20-30 at the restaurant)
meals.dinner: Osteria del Borgo or local trattoria in Poschiavo — Risotto or Polenta dish (~CHF 18-22)

day_by_day.notes: Diavolezza is one of the best value ski areas in the Engadin region. Book ski rental in advance online for discounts. The glacier run is weather and condition dependent — check with ski patrol. Wear sunscreen as Alpine sun reflection off snow is intense even in February.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day from skiing — let your muscles recover. After B&B breakfast, take a scenic snowshoe hike around the Poschiavo valley. Rent snowshoes from a local sports shop (~CHF 15-20/day) or ask the B&B for recommendations. The trail from Poschiavo toward Le Prese along the lake is flat, beautiful, and free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the small village of Le Prese on the southern shore of Lago di Poschiavo — a 20-minute walk or short train ride. Explore the lakeside promenade and enjoy the peaceful winter atmosphere. Stop at a local café for a hot chocolate or espresso. Browse the local Graubünden craft shops for affordable handmade souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo for the evening. Visit the local Coop or Migros to stock up on Swiss chocolate, local cheeses, and Bündnerfleisch (air-dried beef) as affordable gifts. Enjoy a self-catered fondue night at the B&B — buy a fondue kit from the supermarket (~CHF 15-20 for two people) for a classic Swiss experience.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B
meals.lunch: Café in Le Prese — soup and bread or a light snack (~CHF 10-15)
meals.dinner: Self-catered Swiss cheese fondue at the B&B using a supermarket fondue kit (~CHF 15-20 for two) — a fun and authentic budget experience

day_by_day.notes: Ask the B&B host if they have a fondue set you can borrow — many Swiss B&Bs do. The snowshoe trail around the lake is suitable for all fitness levels. Le Prese is a quieter, less touristy alternative to larger resort towns and very budget-friendly.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Bernina Express regional train north to St. Moritz (~45 minutes, ~CHF 12-15 one way). Arrive in the famous resort town and explore on foot — the town center, Via Serlas, and the frozen Lake St. Moritz are free to walk around. Admire the luxury without spending luxury prices. The frozen lake hosts the famous White Turf horse races in February — check if an event is scheduled (free to watch from the lakeside).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the St. Moritz Langlauf (cross-country skiing) trails around the Engadin valley — these are significantly cheaper than downhill skiing. A cross-country ski pass is ~CHF 10-15/day. Alternatively, enjoy free winter activities: ice skating on the natural lake (skate rental ~CHF 8-10), or a free walk up to the Segantini Museum viewpoint for panoramic Engadin valley views.
day_by_day.evening: Before returning to Poschiavo, grab a budget dinner in St. Moritz — head away from the main tourist strip to find more affordable options. Return by regional train to Poschiavo by 20:00-21:00.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B — eat well before the day trip
meals.lunch: Migros or Coop supermarket in St. Moritz — grab a ready-made sandwich, soup, or hot meal from the deli counter (~CHF 8-12) — the most budget-friendly option in expensive St. Moritz
meals.dinner: Pizzeria or casual restaurant in St. Moritz away from the main strip, or pack dinner and eat back at the B&B (~CHF 15-20)

day_by_day.notes: St. Moritz is one of the world's most expensive resorts but can be enjoyed on a budget by focusing on free activities and self-catering for meals. The Migros supermarket in St. Moritz is your best friend for affordable food. Check the White Turf horse racing schedule at whiteturf.ch — if it falls on your visit weekend it is a spectacular free spectacle.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Poschiavo. Enjoy a leisurely last B&B breakfast. Take a final walk through the historic village center and along the river. Visit the local Sunday market if available for local produce and crafts. Pack your bags and check out of the B&B.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight, take the scenic Bernina Express or regional train back toward Tirano (Italy) or north toward Chur and Zurich for your onward journey. The train ride through the Bernina Pass in winter is a perfect final memory — snow-covered viaducts, frozen lakes, and dramatic Alpine peaks. If time allows, stop briefly in Tirano (Italy) just across the border for a final espresso and Italian pastry at a local bar (~€2-3).
day_by_day.evening: Travel to your departure airport. Zurich Airport is approximately 3-4 hours by train from Poschiavo via Chur. Milan Malpensa is approximately 2.5-3 hours via Tirano. Allow plenty of time for connections.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B — enjoy your final Swiss breakfast
meals.lunch: Train station or airport — grab a Migros or Coop to-go meal, or a final Swiss Bratwurst from a station kiosk (~CHF 8-12)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Check train times carefully on SBB.ch the night before — Sunday schedules may differ slightly. The Bernina Pass route can be affected by weather in February — have a backup route via Tirano if needed. Keep CHF coins for luggage lockers at train stations. Confirm your return flight details and allow extra time for Alpine train connections which can occasionally run late in winter weather.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Transfer from airport to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Settle into your room and rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama around 23:30–00:00 depending on transfer. Check in, unpack, and get a good night's sleep to prepare for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit or grab a snack at the airport
meals.dinner: Pick up a light snack or sandwich at Zurich/Milan airport before your transfer, or ask the B&B if a late-night snack basket can be arranged in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange your airport transfer to Poschiavo before departure — the drive from Zurich is approximately 2.5–3 hours, or consider an overnight train via Chur and the Bernina Express route. Confirm late check-in with the B&B. Keep luggage minimal for easy transit.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely start. After a hearty B&B breakfast, take a short orientation walk around the charming village of Poschiavo — explore the historic Piazza Comunale, the Spanish-style houses, and the scenic lakeside of Lago di Poschiavo. Get your bearings and breathe in the crisp Alpine air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby Livigno ski area (approx. 45 min drive via the Forcola di Livigno pass — check seasonal road access) or explore beginner-friendly local slopes around Poschiavo. Alternatively, rent equipment from a local sports shop in Poschiavo and test the gentle cross-country trails along the valley floor as a warm-up day for skiing.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo village for a relaxed first evening. Stroll the old town and enjoy the Romansh-Italian cultural blend of the Valposchiavo region.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — enjoy local bread, cheese, cold cuts, and coffee included with your stay.
meals.lunch: Ristorante Suisse in Poschiavo — a mid-range local restaurant serving hearty Graubünden specialties like pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta) and barley soup. Budget CHF 20–35.
meals.dinner: Osteria Salis in Poschiavo — cozy Italian-Swiss osteria with regional wines and rustic pasta dishes. Budget CHF 35–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Check road conditions for the Forcola di Livigno pass — it may be closed in deep winter. If closed, plan a scenic valley walk instead. Use this day to recover from jet lag and acclimatize to the altitude (Poschiavo sits at ~1,000m). Pick up a local SIM or confirm your mobile data plan works in Switzerland.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on the iconic Bernina Express cogwheel train from Poschiavo station — one of the most scenic rail journeys in the world and a UNESCO World Heritage route. Ride up through dramatic viaducts and glacial landscapes to St. Moritz (approx. 1.5 hours). This is a breathtaking introduction to the high Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon skiing at Corviglia, St. Moritz's main ski area — accessible via funicular from the town center. With 350km of pistes across the Engadin ski region, there's terrain for all levels. Rent equipment at the resort if needed. Enjoy the world-class groomed runs and stunning Engadin valley views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore St. Moritz village before catching the return Bernina Express train to Poschiavo (last trains run in the early evening — check timetable). Alternatively, dine in St. Moritz before heading back.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast before departure — fuel up for a big day.
meals.lunch: Self-service mountain restaurant at Corviglia ski area — try rösti with a fried egg or a warming goulash soup. Budget CHF 20–30.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Casanna in St. Moritz or dine back in Poschiavo at Ristorante Suisse. Mid-range dinner with local Graubünden specialties. Budget CHF 40–60.

day_by_day.notes: Book Bernina Express tickets in advance at sbb.ch — the panoramic cars sell out quickly in ski season. A Swiss Travel Pass may offer discounts. Ski rental in St. Moritz is pricier than in Poschiavo — consider renting locally the day before. Dress in full ski layers as Corviglia sits above 2,500m.

day_by_day.morning: Today is dedicated to the Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Tour. Depart early from Poschiavo by train via the Bernina Express to Chur, then onward to Interlaken and Grindelwald/Lauterbrunnen. Board the cogwheel train to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m — the highest railway station in Europe. Marvel at the Aletsch Glacier, the Sphinx Observatory, and panoramic views across the Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Jungfraujoch — visit the Ice Palace carved inside the glacier, walk the Plateau trail (weather permitting), and enjoy the surreal high-altitude snowscape. This is a once-in-a-lifetime Alpine experience. Begin the descent in the mid-afternoon to avoid the last-train rush.
day_by_day.evening: Given the long travel day, return toward the Interlaken/Grindelwald area and consider an overnight stay there, or begin the return journey to Poschiavo (total travel time is significant — approximately 4–5 hours each way). A smarter option is to book one night in Grindelwald or Interlaken to break the journey.

meals.breakfast: Early B&B breakfast or grab a pastry and coffee at Poschiavo station.
meals.lunch: Restaurant Crystal at Jungfraujoch — self-service cafeteria at the top of Europe. Expect higher prices at altitude (CHF 25–40) but the experience is unmatched.
meals.dinner: If staying in Grindelwald: Restaurant Onkel Tom's Hütte — a beloved mid-range mountain restaurant with fondue and raclette. Budget CHF 40–60. If returning to Poschiavo: Osteria Salis for a late dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Jungfraujoch tickets cost approximately CHF 145–210 depending on departure point — book online at jungfrau.ch for discounts. The Swiss Travel Pass covers part of the journey. Altitude sickness is possible at 3,454m — ascend slowly, stay hydrated, and avoid alcohol at the top. Bring sunglasses and sunscreen as UV radiation is intense at altitude. This is a very long travel day — consider splitting it with an overnight in Grindelwald.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day back to Poschiavo if you stayed overnight in Grindelwald/Interlaken. Alternatively, if you returned the previous evening, enjoy a relaxed morning at the B&B. Then head out for the Zermatt Ski Safari experience — travel by train from Poschiavo via Chur and the Glacier Express route toward Zermatt (approximately 4–5 hours). Zermatt is car-free and accessed by electric taxi or on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the Zermatt Ski Safari — explore the legendary slopes beneath the iconic Matterhorn with access to over 360km of groomed pistes. The ski area connects Switzerland and Italy (Cervinia), offering incredible variety. Focus on the Rothorn and Gornergrat sectors for stunning scenery and well-groomed intermediate runs.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Zermatt's vibrant après-ski scene — the village is one of Switzerland's most atmospheric mountain towns. Explore the car-free streets, browse the shops, and warm up with a Glühwein at a terrace bar. Consider an overnight stay in Zermatt to maximize skiing time tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast or hotel breakfast in Grindelwald if staying over.
meals.lunch: Chez Vrony restaurant on the Findeln piste in Zermatt — a legendary mid-mountain restaurant with stunning Matterhorn views. Try the rösti or the cheese soup. Budget CHF 35–55.
meals.dinner: Swiss Alpine Fondue Evening experience in Zermatt — warm up after a day on the slopes with a traditional Swiss cheese fondue dinner at a cozy mountain chalet restaurant. Try Restaurant du Pont or Walliserkanne for authentic Valais fondue. Budget CHF 45–65.

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt lift passes cost approximately CHF 85–95 per day — book online for slight discounts. The Zermatt ski area is one of the highest in the Alps (up to 3,883m) so dress warmly in layers. Book accommodation in Zermatt in advance if staying overnight — mid-range options include Hotel Romantica or Hotel Walliserhof. The Glacier Express scenic train is an experience in itself — book panoramic seats.

day_by_day.morning: Full day of skiing in Zermatt — continue the Zermatt Ski Safari. Head to the Klein Matterhorn sector (3,883m) for high-altitude glacier skiing and the famous Italian connection to Cervinia. The views of the Matterhorn from the slopes are absolutely iconic. Take the Trockener Steg gondola for access to the best intermediate and advanced terrain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Sunnegga Paradise sector — accessible by underground funicular — for sunny, sheltered slopes and excellent snow conditions. This area is perfect for a mix of cruising runs and scenic stops. If feeling adventurous, try the Kumme mogul field or the Triftji run for a challenge.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return journey to Poschiavo via train (Zermatt → Visp → Chur → Poschiavo via Bernina Express). Alternatively, enjoy one final evening in Zermatt with a celebratory dinner before the early morning return.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Zermatt or grab a fresh croissant and coffee at a village bakery.
meals.lunch: Bergrestaurant Furgg at 2,432m — a classic mountain hut with panoramic views and hearty Alpine food. Try the Älplermagronen (Alpine mac and cheese) or the daily soup. Budget CHF 25–40.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Schäferstube in Zermatt — a cozy, mid-range restaurant with Valais specialties including air-dried beef (Bündnerfleisch) and raclette. Budget CHF 45–65. Or dine back in Poschiavo upon return.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is the busiest day on the slopes — arrive at the lifts early (before 9am) to avoid queues. The Zermatt ski area is vast — download the Zermatt app for real-time piste and lift information. If returning to Poschiavo this evening, check train connections carefully as the Bernina line has limited evening departures. Consider purchasing a souvenir Matterhorn photo from the summit photographers.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning back in Poschiavo. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the B&B and take a peaceful farewell walk around Lago di Poschiavo — the lake is often partially frozen in February, creating a magical winter landscape. Reflect on the week's adventures with the Bernina peaks as your backdrop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pack and check out of B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. If time allows before your departure transfer, visit the local Poschiavo market (Sunday markets are seasonal — check locally) or browse the village's artisan shops for Swiss chocolate, local cheese, and Graubünden specialties to bring home as gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to your departure airport (Zurich approx. 3 hours, Milan Malpensa approx. 2.5 hours). Enjoy a final Swiss meal at the airport or en route. Depart Switzerland with incredible memories of the Alps.

meals.breakfast: Final full B&B breakfast — savor the local cheeses, homemade jams, and fresh bread one last time.
meals.lunch: Café/Pasticceria Roncaioli in Poschiavo — a charming local café with Italian-Swiss pastries, panini, and excellent coffee. Budget CHF 15–25. Perfect for a light farewell lunch.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or a roadside stop at a Swiss motorway service area — try a final Bratwurst with mustard and a Rivella soda for a quintessentially Swiss send-off. Budget CHF 20–35.

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for your departure transfer — road conditions in February can be unpredictable due to snow. Confirm your transfer booking 24 hours in advance. Duty-free Swiss chocolate at the airport makes excellent gifts. Ensure ski equipment rentals are returned before checkout. Keep your Swiss Travel Pass or rail tickets as a memento — they make great souvenirs!

Rent premium ski equipment at a top-tier rental shop in Livigno (e.g., Intersport Livigno or Mottolino Ski Rental). Livigno offers 115km of slopes across all levels.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by early evening. Freshen up at the B&B, then enjoy a premium dinner at Ristorante Suisse in Poschiavo — a refined local restaurant offering Graubünden specialties including Pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta with cheese and vegetables), venison ragù, and an excellent regional wine list.

meals.breakfast: Full Alpine breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — freshly baked bread, local honey, mountain butter, cold cuts, regional cheeses, soft-boiled eggs, fresh fruit, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant lunch on the Livigno slopes — try Ristorante Mottolino or Tea del Vidal for hearty Alpine cuisine: polenta with cheese, goulash soup, and mulled wine.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Suisse, Poschiavo — multi-course dinner featuring Graubünden regional cuisine. Recommended: Capuns (chard-wrapped dumplings), slow-braised venison, and a bottle of local Malanser Pinot Noir.

day_by_day.notes: Livigno is technically in Italy but is easily accessible from Poschiavo and offers duty-free shopping — a bonus for luxury gear or Swiss watches. Confirm ski rental reservations in advance. Dress in high-performance ski layers; February temperatures on the slopes can range from -5°C to -15°C.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast at the B&B, then depart for a full-day Zermatt Ski Safari experience. Take a private luxury transfer or drive to Zermatt (approximately 2.5 hours from Poschiavo). Arrive in Zermatt — a car-free village — and transfer to your ski locker via electric taxi. Begin the Zermatt Ski Safari: explore the legendary slopes with access to over 360km of groomed pistes beneath the iconic Matterhorn. Start with the Rothorn and Sunnegga Paradise sectors for panoramic morning light on the Matterhorn.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Zermatt Ski Safari into the Klein Matterhorn (Matterhorn Glacier Paradise) sector — the highest ski area in the Alps at 3,883m. Ski the glacier runs with breathtaking 360-degree views across Switzerland, Italy, and France. Optionally, cross into Cervinia, Italy, for a run on the Italian side of the Matterhorn.
day_by_day.evening: Wind down in Zermatt village. Enjoy a premium après-ski experience at the Vernissage Bar or Cervo Mountain Resort's lounge. Dinner at Chez Vrony — one of Zermatt's most celebrated mountain restaurants, perched above the village with direct Matterhorn views. Return to Poschiavo by private transfer after dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full Alpine breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Findlerhof Restaurant on the Sunnegga slopes — a legendary Zermatt mountain hut known for its Rösti, raclette, and stunning Matterhorn panorama. Reserve in advance.
meals.dinner: Chez Vrony, Zermatt — award-winning Alpine cuisine. Signature dishes include Valais beef tartare, truffle Rösti, and locally sourced lamb. Exceptional Swiss wine cellar. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt is a highlight of any Swiss Alps trip. Book the Zermatt Ski Safari guide in advance through the Zermatt Ski School or a luxury concierge service. Zermatt is car-free — arrange an electric taxi from the Täsch parking area or take the Matterhorn Gotthard Bahn train from Täsch. Lift passes for Zermatt are premium-priced; purchase the 'Zermatt Unlimited' pass for full access.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early from Poschiavo for the Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Tour (approximately 3 hours drive to Grindelwald/Lauterbrunnen valley). Board the cogwheel train from Grindelwald Terminal or Lauterbrunnen, ascending through the Eiger and Mönch to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m — the highest railway station in Europe. Explore the Ice Palace, the Sphinx Observatory, and the eternal snow plateau with views of the Aletsch Glacier, the longest glacier in the Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Jungfraujoch experience, descend to Grindelwald First ski area for an afternoon of skiing on the First plateau (2,168m). Enjoy well-groomed intermediate and advanced runs with iconic views of the Eiger North Face. Alternatively, try the First Flyer zipline or First Cliff Walk for a thrilling non-ski adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed après-ski in Grindelwald village before the drive back to Poschiavo. Dinner at Restaurant Schmitte in Grindelwald — a cozy, upscale Alpine restaurant known for its cheese fondue, raclette, and Bernese specialties. Return to Poschiavo by private transfer.

meals.breakfast: Full Alpine breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Crystal Restaurant at Jungfraujoch (3,454m) — a unique dining experience at the Top of Europe. Enjoy hot soups, Swiss specialties, and panoramic glacier views.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Schmitte, Grindelwald — traditional Bernese Oberland cuisine. Recommended: classic Swiss cheese fondue for two, Bernese platter, and a carafe of Fendant white wine.

day_by_day.notes: The Jungfraujoch train tickets must be booked well in advance, especially in peak February season. Purchase the 'Jungfrau Travel Pass' for best value. The altitude at Jungfraujoch (3,454m) can cause mild altitude sickness — stay hydrated and ascend slowly. Dress in very warm layers; temperatures at the summit can reach -20°C with wind chill.

day_by_day.morning: Depart from Poschiavo for Verbier (approximately 3 hours drive). Arrive in Verbier — one of the world's premier ski resorts and freeride capitals. Begin the Verbier Freeride Experience with a certified IFMGA mountain guide. Start with a safety briefing, avalanche transceiver check, and route planning. Head to the iconic Lac des Vaux and Mont Gelé sectors for guided off-piste freeride runs through pristine powder fields and natural terrain features.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Verbier Freeride Experience into the afternoon. Explore the legendary Vallon d'Arby couloir or the Stairway to Heaven off-piste route (guide-dependent on snow conditions). The 4 Vallées ski area offers 412km of terrain — one of the largest ski domains in the world. Take a break at a mountain refuge for hot chocolate and energy snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski at Farinet Bar in Verbier — the iconic après-ski institution with live music and a vibrant atmosphere. Dinner at La Grange restaurant in Verbier — a legendary Alpine dining institution known for its raclette, fondue, and Valais specialties in a rustic-chic chalet setting. Return to Poschiavo by private transfer.

meals.breakfast: Full Alpine breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Cabane du Mont Fort (2,457m) — a classic Swiss Alpine hut above Verbier with hearty mountain cuisine: lentil soup, cheese Rösti, and hot fruit teas. Spectacular views of the Grand Combin massif.
meals.dinner: La Grange, Verbier — iconic Valais dining experience. Signature dishes: Valais raclette with cornichons and potatoes, air-dried beef (Viande séchée), and Valais Pinot Noir. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: The Verbier Freeride Experience requires intermediate-to-advanced skiing ability and physical fitness. Book a certified IFMGA guide through Verbier's Bureau des Guides or a luxury ski concierge. Avalanche safety equipment (transceiver, probe, shovel) is mandatory and typically provided by the guide. Check snow and avalanche conditions the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: A more relaxed morning — enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast at the B&B. Then drive or take the Rhaetian Railway (Bernina Express route) from Poschiavo toward Davos (approximately 2 hours by train — a UNESCO World Heritage scenic journey). Arrive in Davos — the highest city in Europe at 1,560m. Begin the Davos Cross-Country Skiing & Nordic Trail experience: glide through 100km of perfectly groomed Nordic trails around the Davos valley. Start with the scenic Davos Lake loop trail — flat and picturesque for a morning warm-up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue Nordic skiing on the Flüela or Sertig valley trails — more challenging routes through pristine Alpine forests and open meadows. Alternatively, explore the Davos Parsenn ski area for a few downhill runs — one of Switzerland's largest and most historic ski resorts with 320km of pistes. The Weissfluhjoch sector offers spectacular panoramic runs.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the Swiss Alpine Fondue Evening experience in Davos — warm up after a day on the trails with a traditional Swiss cheese fondue dinner at a cozy mountain chalet restaurant. Recommended: Restaurant Bolgenschanze or Hubli's Landhaus in Davos for an authentic, premium fondue experience with local Appenzeller and Gruyère cheese blend. Return to Poschiavo by private transfer or scenic night train.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent full Alpine breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — take your time this morning.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bergrestaurant Schatzalp in Davos — a historic Art Nouveau mountain hotel restaurant accessible by funicular. Enjoy panoramic views over Davos while dining on Alpine classics: mushroom risotto, veal escalope, and regional wines.
meals.dinner: Swiss Alpine Fondue Evening at Hubli's Landhaus, Davos — a premium fondue and raclette experience in a beautifully restored historic chalet. Features moitié-moitié fondue (Gruyère & Vacherin), truffle raclette, and an extensive Swiss wine list.

day_by_day.notes: The Bernina Express train from Poschiavo is a world-class scenic experience in itself — book first-class panoramic car seats in advance through SBB (Swiss Federal Railways). Nordic ski equipment rental is available at Davos Sport shops. The Davos Cross-Country trails are free to use with a valid Nordic pass. February in Davos can be very cold (-10°C to -20°C) — dress in high-performance Nordic layers.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps — enjoy a leisurely, celebratory farewell breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Take a final scenic walk around Lake Poschiavo or through the village to soak in the last views of the Bernina massif and surrounding peaks. Visit the local Poschiavo market (Sunday morning) for artisan cheeses, local honey, and Graubünden specialties to take home as souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure logistics, enjoy a final half-day ski session at Livigno (45 minutes away) — a perfect, relaxed farewell to the slopes. Alternatively, take a scenic drive over the Bernina Pass (2,328m) — one of the most spectacular Alpine road crossings — stopping at Lago Bianco for photographs of the frozen lake and surrounding glaciers. Begin the journey toward your departure airport.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Ristorante La Romantica in Poschiavo or at a premium restaurant en route to the airport. Celebrate an extraordinary week in the Swiss Alps with a final glass of Graubünden Pinot Noir and a dessert of Torta di Pane (traditional Poschiavo bread cake). Depart for home with memories of world-class skiing, breathtaking Alpine scenery, and exceptional Swiss hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell Alpine breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — request a special spread with local specialties: Graubünden Nusstorte, Bündnerfleisch (air-dried beef), regional cheeses, and fresh pastries.
meals.lunch: Light mountain lunch at a Livigno slope restaurant or a picnic with provisions from the Poschiavo market — local cheese, cured meats, sourdough, and Swiss chocolate.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Ristorante La Romantica, Poschiavo — intimate, candlelit setting with refined Graubünden cuisine. Recommended: homemade pasta with truffle, braised local beef, and a bottle of Malanser Pinot Noir to toast the journey.

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for the transfer to your departure airport — Zurich (approx. 3 hours) or Milan Malpensa (approx. 2 hours) from Poschiavo. Pre-arrange a private luxury transfer for a stress-free departure. Pack any purchased souvenirs carefully — Swiss cheeses and cured meats may have customs restrictions depending on your destination country. Consider purchasing a Swiss Rail Pass or Bernina Express souvenir ticket as a memento of the journey.
